subject: Micro-commit addendum and pro-rata surge invoice structure
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@feldspar.ai>

Cc: proc@feldspar.ai, j.ellis@feldspar.ai
Date: 2028-04-29T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Billing structure for May launch spike (PO draft attached)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Our engineering team confirmed the new feature will go live the week of May 6th and we expect a fairly sharp traffic spike in the first 48 hours (projected delta: ~5-6x baseline for 36 hours).

Procurement asked me to share a PO draft so we can lock the billing path quickly. Two asks from our side:
- Is there a way to avoid unpredictable one-off overrun invoices that could blow our credit card limits?
- Can we get a predictable split so our finance team can reconcile: a single monthly base invoice plus a separate line (weekly true-up) for bursts?

I've attached a PO draft and a high-level traffic estimate. If you can outline options and a recommended approach we can route it through legal/procurement immediately.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that's easier.

Best,
Alice
Head of Platform
Feldspar AI

Attachment: feldspar_po_draft.pdf (application/pdf)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@feldspar.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-29T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing structure for May launch spike (PO draft attached)

Alice — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick proposal that should give Feldspar the predictability you need while letting you scale for the short window:

Proposal (summary):
1) Micro-commit addendum: a short-term baseline commit for May (e.g., 5M token-equivalent) priced at your negotiated committed rate. This covers most steady-state usage.
2) Surge ladder for bursts: bursts above the baseline will be billed on a stepped overrun schedule (Tier A/B/C) where unit price decreases as cumulative burst consumption grows during the billing period. This avoids a single punitive overrun rate.
3) Split invoicing:
   - Monthly base invoice: commit + standard monthly usage under commit.
   - Weekly burst true-ups: a lightweight weekly line item that captures Surge ladder usage and any tier transitions. Final reconciliation in month-end invoice.
4) Pre-funded buffer (optional): you can pre-fund a small burst buffer (one-time credit) that will be drawn first; any remaining burst usage follows the Surge ladder. If you convert to a longer commit within 6 months, a portion of the buffer can be credited back as a conversion incentive.

Numbers — illustrative only (we'll finalize after you confirm expected delta):
- Baseline commit (5M tokens) at $0.004/token
- Surge ladder: Tier A (0-500k over baseline): $0.006/token; Tier B (500k-2.5M): $0.005/token; Tier C (>2.5M): $0.0045/token
- Pre-funded buffer: $10k credit (drawn down, non-refundable; 50% credited on 6-month commit conversion)

Next steps I propose:
- Ben (cc'ed) will confirm the exact ladder pricing and any legal language required in an amendment.
- Laura (cc'ed, finance) will confirm the billing flow and whether weekly true-ups are okay for your AP team.
- If Feldspar agrees in principle, we'll draft a short addendum (1-2 pages) and route to DocuSign.

I've also attached a recent usage snapshot to validate the tiers against your estimate.

If you want to run a quick scenario call today or tomorrow, I'm available after 1pm PT.

—Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage_snapshot_Mar2028.csv (text/csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@feldspar.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-30T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing structure for May launch spike (PO draft attached) — surge ladder refinement

Thanks Olga — adding a few operational clarifications and an alternative that Procurement sometimes prefers.

Operational refinements:
- Weekly true-ups will be posted as provisional line items; finalized at month end once usage reconciles. We can export a CSV each Monday for your AP—same format as the attached snapshot.
- To protect against card limits, we can send an invoice run on the 1st that includes commit + any finalized burst amounts from the previous week. That keeps mid-month spikes from hitting the card unexpectedly.

Alternative: pre-authorized headroom (preferred for fast launches)
- Feldspar pre-authorizes a headroom amount (suggest $25k) on the PO. We only capture funds if weekly true-ups exceed thresholds. Pre-authorized funds are held against the account and reduce the chance of failed payments during a launch. If unused, they expire and are not captured.

Discount for conversion option:
- If Feldspar signs a 6-month committed conversion within 60 days of the launch, we will apply a 12% credit against burst charges incurred during the initial month (applied as a single credit line on the first post-conversion invoice).

Payment and legal notes:
- Laura: confirm appropriate GL codes and whether weekly provisional lines can route to your AP team for internal matching.
- Once Feldspar confirms, Legal will prepare the amendment. We typically keep language minimal: term, ladder, buffer, and conversion credit clause.

Alice — can you confirm Procurement's preference for: (A) weekly true-ups + month-end reconciliation, or (B) pre-authorized headroom? Also let us know if your PO needs the amendment referenced as an attachment (we can provide a DocuSign-ready PDF).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@feldspar.ai>

Please send the DocuSign link and the amendment PDF and we'll get this routed. If it's helpful I can be on a 15-minute call at 4:30pm PT to sign off final wording.

Thanks — Alice
